catalog_quote: [Anderson & Ross 2002: 323, sec. 1.2 Phonotactics and stress] The syllable structure is (C)V(N). Where two vowels occur in sequence, these belong to separate syllables. ... Stress is predictable, falling on the penultimate syllable. [Sheppard 2020: 51] Syllable structure is (C)V(N). The labialised, prenasalised, and prenasalised labialised consonants are analysed as unit phonemes and there are no consonant clusters. Stress is not always predictable; however, it frequently falls on the penultimate syllable (or the antepenultimate syllable, if the penultimate syllable contains a schwa). [Sheppard 2020: 133-134] Study of a reasonable sample of bound VC morphemes from the corpus using the Praat software package indicates that they show variation in stress patterning as well. new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress on the penultimate syllable; when the penult contains schwa (orthographic ɨ) stress retracts to the antepenult; the author flags that stress is not fully predictable. The SIL OPD (Andersons 1992, p.5) independently states the same: stress probably not phonemic, usually penultimate, heavy syllables with a diphthong tend to attract stress, and stress shifts leftward off a syllable containing /ɨ/.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either source.
new_statements.exceptions: Penult with schwa /ɨ/ -> antepenultimate stress (both sources); heavy (diphthong) syllables tend to be stressed (OPD); 'not always predictable' residue (both). Sheppard pp.133-134: in the verb complex, object indexes are never stressed, transitive/applicative =nga, =wana can be, and stem stress shifts depending on which bound morphemes are present.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a phonology overview; Sheppard separately describes clause intonation (declarative fall, polar-question rise on penult). Verb-complex clitic/affix stress behaviour treated as unresolved.
new_statements.identity_note: Both quoted sources describe Sudest as spoken on Vanatɨna (Sudest/Tagula) Island; the SIL OPD names Pamela village (Andersons' SIL base); Sheppard's fieldwork was on Vanatɨna and Yeina islands. Same languoid, sude1239; no dialect split relevant to the stress statement.
